summary: Largely clean on the design dimension. The 42 near-identical 3-line wrappers look like copy-paste duplication, but that exact @proxy/_call_lib_func form is the repo's documented binding convention (CLAUDE.md 'Adding a New Binding') and a factory/loop would break both the @proxy cache anchor (which keys on the decorated function's inspect.getfile/co_firstlineno) and the per-function automodule docs, so it is intentional and not reported as a defect. Signatures, argument names (incl. atan2(y, x)), and __all__ are all consistent. One genuine low-severity design hazard: the public star-imported surface re-exports wrappers named after the Python builtins round and pow, shadowing them in numbox.core.bindings.

findings.title: Wrappers named 'round' and 'pow' shadow Python builtins in the star-imported public namespace
findings.claim: _math.__all__ lists 'round' and 'pow', and numbox/core/bindings/__init__.py does 'from numbox.core.bindings._math import *'. So 'from numbox.core.bindings import *' (or attribute access on the package) rebinds the names round and pow to the libm wrappers, shadowing the Python builtins. A caller who does the star-import and then writes round(x) / pow(a, b) at module scope silently gets the libm-semantics single/two-arg float64 wrappers (e.g. round half-away-from-zero, pow with no 3-arg modular form) instead of the builtins, and pow/round on non-float arguments will now hit the wrapper's float64 signature. This is a maintenance/misuse hazard rather than a correctness bug in the wrappers themselves.
findings.evidence: _math.py line 14: '"ceil", "floor", "trunc", "round", "rint", "nearbyint",' and line 18: '"pow", "fmod", "remainder",' place both names in __all__. Definitions at lines 152-154 ('def round(x): return _call_lib_func("round", (x,))') and 197-199 ('def pow(x, y): return _call_lib_func("pow", (x, y))'). __init__.py line 2: 'from numbox.core.bindings._math import * # noqa: F401, F403'. Per CLAUDE.md, 'Anything at top level without a leading underscore is part of the public API.'
findings.recommendation: This is in tension with the documented rule 'Function names must match the C library names exactly,' so renaming the wrappers is not warranted. Lowest-risk mitigation: document the shadowing explicitly (a note in docs/numbox.core.bindings.rst and/or a comment near __all__) so consumers know that star-importing the bindings package overrides round/pow, and prefer 'import numbox.core.bindings as nbm; nbm.round(...)' over star-import. No code change to the wrappers is recommended.
